events.description: Five jihadi groups, led by Hurras al-Din, announced the Stand Firm operations room.
Abu Hamam al-Shami met Omar al-Shishani while mediating between al-Nusra and ISIS.
Abu Hamam appeared in a video describing his truce efforts between al-Nusra and ISIS.
Julani rebranded Nusra as Jabhat Fatah al-Sham, breaking from al-Qaeda; Abu Hamam publicly objected and left.
Nusra rebranded again as Hayat Tahrir al-Sham after merging with other factions; Saif al-Adel and Abu Muhammad al-Masri objected, and the coalition later broke apart.
Al-Qaeda's global network established a reconciliation initiative for the Syrian infighting, overseen by Abu Abdul Karim al-Masri.
HTS and Hurras al-Din reached an accord in early 2018, followed by another bout of infighting later in 2018.
Long War Journal published an analysis of Karim's role in the HTS–Hurras al-Din accord.
US State Department offered a reward of up to $5 million for Abu Abdul Karim al-Masri.
HTS arrested several figures linked to the new operations room, including a military commander, Abu Salah al-Uzbeki and an alleged British aid worker.
HTS and the Stand Firm room reportedly agreed to stand down around recording time.
Sami al-Oreidi released a video warning jihadis against dependence on others, a critique of HTS reliance on Turkey.
Imran Khan called Osama bin Laden a martyr killed in Abbottabad.
Rifai Taha Ahmed Musa was killed by a US drone after entering Idlib from Turkey (date not stated in the transcript).
Tom Joscelyn testified before Congress about senior al-Qaeda operatives enjoying de facto Turkish protection.
Rifai Ahmed Taha Musa was killed by a US drone soon after arriving in Idlib from Turkey.
Abu Omar al-Baghdadi and Abu Hamza al-Muhajir, leaders of the Islamic State of Iraq, were killed.
AQAP ruled large areas of southern Yemen for about a year (2010-11).
Nusra Front rebranded and disassociated from al-Qaeda as Jabhat Fatah al-Sham, approved by Abu al-Khayr al-Masri in an audio message.
Abu al-Khayr al-Masri, Zawahiri's deputy, was killed in a US drone strike using an R-9X missile in Idlib.
Imran Khan told Pakistan's National Assembly that Osama bin Laden had been 'martyred' in Abbottabad and criticized the US.
State Department released Country Reports on Terrorism for 2019, saying Pakistan continued to serve as a safe haven for certain regionally focused terrorist groups.
Al-Shabaab killed American member Omar Hammami after about 18 months of public disputes (year not stated in transcript).
Lashkar-e-Taiba suicide assault on Mumbai killed over 160 people; Sajid Mir was the mastermind
Jaish-e-Mohammed attack in Jammu and Kashmir killed 40 Indian police
Khalilzad recommended that Congress designate Pakistan a state sponsor of terrorism
Tom Joscelyn testified to the House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Intelligence and Counterterrorism alongside Mike Morell
Trump gave a West Point graduation speech about ending the endless wars

key_claims: Syria is al-Qaeda's most unstable platform, with repeated infighting since 2016 among its own affiliates and allies rather than only with ISIS.
The central dispute between HTS and Hurras al-Din is HTS's reliance on Turkey in Idlib and the public perception of dependence on a state, not a split over global jihad strategy.
Abu Hamam al-Shami, a pre-9/11 al-Faruq camp trainer, leads Hurras al-Din and was among the first to reject Julani's July 2016 break with al-Qaeda.
Senior al-Qaeda leaders Saif al-Adel and Abu Muhammad al-Masri, based in Iran, also objected to Julani's rebrandings.
Abu Abdul Karim al-Masri, a Shura Council member, oversaw al-Qaeda's 2017-2018 reconciliation effort between HTS and Hurras al-Din, with branches in Somalia, Mali and the Maghreb backing it.
Senior al-Qaeda operatives such as Muhammad Islambouli and Rifai Taha have enjoyed de facto Turkish protection, though Rifai Taha was killed by a US drone once he entered Idlib.
Each reconciliation between the two sides is likely temporary, and the Stand Firm room signals underlying tensions.
Al-Qaeda has made deals with states (Mauritania, Pakistan, Iran), so dealing with Turkey is not forbidden, but the degree and visibility of dependence is the problem.
Al-Qaeda senior leadership and HTS under Julani are in a leadership dispute over Turkish protection and holding territory in Idlib; al-Qaeda has not publicly disowned Julani.
Al-Qaeda's actual chain of command in Syria is opaque since the July 2016 rebranding, with figures such as Karim, Muhaysini and Hurras al-Din's Abu Humam complicating the picture.
Senior al-Qaeda operatives have enjoyed de facto Turkish protection, and Turkey's relationship with HTS mirrors Pakistan's relationship with the Taliban.
US drone strikes have removed al-Qaeda veterans who could act as a counterweight to Julani, but the hosts argue they are too slow to cause decisive infighting.
The hosts judge al-Qaeda's senior leadership right that holding territory in Idlib is unsustainable against the Assad-Russia-Iran coalition.

The 2019 State Department terrorism report acknowledges Pakistan as a safe haven for the Taliban, Haqqani Network, LeT and JeM; the hosts argue calling them 'regionally focused' understates their role in sustaining al-Qaeda.
The hosts regard Pakistan and Iran as leading state sponsors of terrorism, with Turkey rising to be the third.
The hosts argue that labeling LeT, JeM and the Taliban 'regionally focused' understates their links to al-Qaeda's global network.
Pakistan redirects India-focused groups such as LeT and JeM to support the Taliban in Afghanistan when pressure from India rises.
Groups in Pakistan serve as feeder organizations for al-Qaeda and ISIS, forming the 'wheel of jihad'.
Pakistan's strategy of riding the tiger produced the TTP insurgency, which killed tens of thousands of Pakistanis.
Pakistan, with parts of the ISI ideologically invested, views the Taliban as a counterweight to India.
Al-Qaeda is reportedly helping the Taliban fight ISIS in eastern Afghanistan, so US reliance on the Taliban against ISIS effectively makes al-Qaeda a de facto ally.
The State report says Masood Azhar and Sajid Mir live in Pakistan under state protection, yet Pakistan has not been designated a state sponsor of terrorism.
